column1: It is a great deal easier to motivate employees in a growing organisation than a declining one.
column2: 在不断壮大的组织里激励员工，比在日渐衰退的组织里容易得多。
column3: a great deal easier|容易得多
column6: growing organisation|n. 不断壮大的组织

column1: When organisations are expanding and adding personnel, promotional opportunities, pay rises, and the excitement of being associated with a dynamic organisation create feelings of optimism.
column2: 组织扩大规模、增聘人员时，晋升机会、加薪，以及身为一个充满活力的组织中的一员所带来的兴奋感，都会使人产生乐观情绪。
column8: dynamic organisation|n. 充满活力的组织

column1: Management is able to use the growth to entice and encourage employees.
column2: 管理层可以利用组织的发展来吸引员工、激励员工。

column1: When an organisation is shrinking, the best and most mobile workers are prone to leave voluntarily.
column2: 当组织规模缩小时，最优秀、也最能另谋职位的员工往往会主动离职。

column1: Unfortunately, they are the ones the organisation can least afford to lose – those with the highest skills and experience.
column2: 可惜，技能最高、经验最丰富的这些人，恰恰是组织最经不起失去的人。
column5: can least afford to lose|最经不起失去

column1: The minor employees remain because their job options are limited.
column2: 职位较低的员工会留下来，因为他们可以选择的工作有限。
column3: minor employees|n. 职位较低的员工

column1: Morale also suffers during decline.
column2: 企业走下坡路时，员工士气也会受挫。

column1: People fear they may be the next to be made redundant.
column2: 人们担心自己可能就是下一个被裁掉的人。
column6: be made redundant|因岗位裁撤而失业

column1: Productivity often suffers, as employees spend their time sharing rumours and providing one another with moral support rather than focusing on their jobs.
column2: 生产率往往也会下降，因为员工把时间用来交流传闻、相互打气，很难专心工作。

column1: For those whose jobs are secure, pay increases are rarely possible.
column2: 即便是工作有保障的人，也很少有加薪的可能。

column1: Pay cuts, unheard of during times of growth, may even be imposed.
column2: 企业发展时期闻所未闻的降薪，此时甚至可能被强制推行。

column1: The challenge to management is how to motivate employees under such retrenchment conditions.
column2: 管理层面临的挑战是，在这种紧缩局面下该如何激励员工。
column7: retrenchment|n. 紧缩开支；缩减规模

column1: The ways of meeting this challenge can be broadly divided into six Key Points, which are outlined below.
column2: 应对这一挑战的做法大体上可以归为六个要点，下面逐一概述。
column3: meeting this challenge|应对这一挑战

column1: There is an abundance of evidence to support the motivational benefits that result from carefully matching people to jobs.
column2: 大量证据表明，经过仔细考虑使员工与岗位相匹配，确实有助于激励员工。
column6: motivational benefits|在激励方面的好处
column8: matching people to jobs|使人和岗位相匹配

column1: For example, if the job is running a small business or an autonomous unit within a larger business, high achievers should be sought.
column2: 例如，如果岗位需要经营一家小企业，或管理大企业内部一个自主运营的部门，就应物色成就动机强的人。

column1: However, if the job to be filled is a managerial post in a large bureaucratic organisation, a candidate who has a high need for power and a low need for affiliation should be selected.
column2: 不过，如果要填补的是大型科层制组织中的管理职位，就应选择权力需求高、归属需求低的候选人。
column3: job to be filled|待填补的职位
column7: need for power|对权力的需求
column8: need for affiliation|与他人建立归属关系的需求

column1: Accordingly, high achievers should not be put into jobs that are inconsistent with their needs.
column2: 因此，不应把成就动机强的人安排在与其需要不相符的岗位上。
column5: put into jobs|安排到岗位上

column1: High achievers will do best when the job provides moderately challenging goals and where there is independence and feedback.
column2: 成就出众的员工，在目标具有适度挑战性、工作有自主权且能得到反馈时，表现最好。
column3: High achievers|n. 成就出众的人
column6: challenging goals|n. 有挑战性的目标

column1: However, it should be remembered that not everybody is motivated by jobs that are high in independence, variety and responsibility.
column2: 不过要记住，自主性强、内容多样、责任重的工作，并不能激励所有人。

column1: The literature on goal-setting theory suggests that managers should ensure that all employees have specific goals and receive comments on how well they are doing in those goals.
column2: 有关目标设定理论的文献指出，管理者应确保每位员工都有明确的目标，并能得到反馈，了解自己的目标完成得怎样。
column9: how well they are doing|他们做得怎么样

column1: For those with high achievement needs, typically a minority in any organisation, the existence of external goals is less important because high achievers are already internally motivated.
column2: 成就需求强烈的人在任何组织里通常都是少数。对他们来说，外部目标没那么重要，因为他们本来就有内在动力。
column3: high achievement needs|n. 强烈的成就需求
column8: high achievers|n. 成就出众的人
column9: internally motivated|adj. 有内在动力的

column1: The next factor to be determined is whether the goals should be assigned by a manager or collectively set in conjunction with the employees.
column2: 接下来要确定的是，目标应由管理者指派，还是应由管理者与员工一起制定。

column1: The answer to that depends on perceptions of goal acceptance and the organisation’s culture.
column2: 这取决于人们如何看待员工对目标的接受程度，也取决于组织文化。
column5: goal acceptance|n. 对目标的接受程度

column1: If resistance to goals is expected, the use of participation in goal-setting should increase acceptance.
column2: 如果预计员工会抵触这些目标，让他们参与目标制定，应当能提高他们对目标的接受程度。
column3: resistance to goals|n. 对目标的抵触

column1: If participation is inconsistent with the culture, however, goals should be assigned.
column2: 不过，如果让员工参与制定目标与组织文化不合，就应由管理者直接指定目标。

column1: If participation and the culture are incongruous, employees are likely to perceive the participation process as manipulative and be negatively affected by it.
column2: 如果员工参与的做法与组织文化格格不入，他们很可能觉得这个过程是在操控自己，并因此受到负面影响。

column1: Regardless of whether goals are achievable or well within management’s perceptions of the employee’s ability, if employees see them as unachievable they will reduce their effort.
column2: 无论目标实际上能否达到，也不管管理层是否认定目标完全在员工的能力范围内，只要员工自己觉得做不到，他们投入的努力就会减少。

column1: Managers must be sure, therefore, that employees feel confident that their efforts can lead to performance goals.
column2: 因此，管理者必须确保员工相信，自己的努力能够帮助他们达到绩效目标。

column1: For managers, this means that employees must have the capability of doing the job and must regard the appraisal process as valid.
column2: 对管理者来说，这意味着员工必须有能力胜任工作，也必须认可绩效考评程序的有效性。

column1: Since employees have different needs, what acts as a reinforcement for one may not for another.
column2: 员工的需求各不相同，因此能对一个人的行为起强化作用的东西，对另一个人未必有效。

column1: Managers could use their knowledge of each employee to personalise the rewards over which they have control.
column2: 管理者可以根据自己对每位员工的了解，因人而异地安排自己有权决定的奖励。

column1: Some of the more obvious rewards that managers allocate include pay, promotions, autonomy, job scope and depth, and the opportunity to participate in goal-setting and decision-making.
column2: 管理者给予的奖励中，比较明显的有薪酬、晋升、自主权、工作的范围和深度，以及参与制定目标和决策的机会。
column8: job scope and depth|n. 工作的范围和深度

column1: Managers need to make rewards contingent on performance.
column2: 管理者需要让奖励取决于工作表现。

column1: To reward factors other than performance will only reinforce those other factors.
column2: 如果奖励的是绩效以外的因素，被强化的就只会是那些因素。

column1: Key rewards such as pay increases and promotions or advancements should be allocated for the attainment of the employee’s specific goals.
column2: 加薪、升职或其他职业发展机会等重要奖励，应在员工实现其具体目标时给予。

column1: Consistent with maximising the impact of rewards, managers should look for ways to increase their visibility.
column2: 为了让奖励发挥最大作用，管理者应设法让这些奖励更容易被员工看到。

column1: Eliminating the secrecy surrounding pay by openly communicating everyone’s remuneration, publicising performance bonuses and allocating annual salary increases in a lump sum rather than spreading them out over an entire year are examples of actions that will make rewards more visible and potentially more motivating.
column2: 公布每个人的薪酬，让薪资透明；公开绩效奖金；一次性发放每年的加薪额，而不将其分摊到一整年。这些做法都能使奖励更加显眼，也可能更有激励作用。
column8: annual salary increases|n. 年度加薪额

column1: The way rewards are distributed should be transparent so that employees perceive that rewards or outcomes are equitable and equal to the inputs given.
column2: 奖励的分配方式应当透明，让员工感觉到所得的回报或结果是公平的，与自己的付出相称。

column1: On a simplistic level, experience, abilities, effort and other obvious inputs should explain differences in pay, responsibility and other obvious outcomes.
column2: 简单地说，经验、能力、努力等显而易见的投入，应该能够解释员工在薪酬、所负责任等方面为何有不同的结果。
column3: on a simplistic level|简单地说

column1: The problem, however, is complicated by the existence of dozens of inputs and outcomes and by the fact that employee groups place different degrees of importance on them.
column2: 不过，投入和回报有几十种之多，而且不同员工群体对它们的重视程度并不相同，这使问题更加复杂。
column8: degrees of importance|n. 重视程度

column1: For instance, a study comparing clerical and production workers identified nearly twenty inputs and outcomes.
column2: 例如，一项比较文职人员和生产人员的研究识别出了将近二十项投入与回报。

column1: The clerical workers considered factors such as quality of work performed and job knowledge near the top of their list, but these were at the bottom of the production workers’ list.
column2: 文职人员把工作完成的质量和岗位知识等因素排在很靠前的位置，而生产工人却把这些因素排在末尾。
column5: quality of work performed|n. 工作完成的质量

column1: Similarly, production workers thought that the most important inputs were intelligence and personal involvement with task accomplishment, two factors that were quite low in the importance ratings of the clerks.
column2: 同样，生产工人认为，最重要的投入是智力和亲自参与任务的完成，而在文职人员看来，这两项的重要性却排得相当靠后。

column1: There were also important, though less dramatic, differences on the outcome side.
column2: 在回报方面，两组人也有重要分歧，只是差异没有那么明显。
column7: on the outcome side|在回报方面

column1: For example, production workers rated advancement very highly, whereas clerical workers rated advancement in the lower third of their list.
column2: 例如，生产人员把职业晋升看得很重，而文职人员却把它排在清单末尾的三分之一。
column9: the lower third|排在末尾的三分之一

column1: Such findings suggest that one person’s equity is another’s inequity, so an ideal should probably weigh different inputs and outcomes according to employee group.
column2: 这些发现表明，一人眼中的公平，换一个人看来可能就不公平。因此，理想的做法或许是针对不同员工群体，给各项投入和回报赋予不同权重。
